Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.manager

Class DatabaseManager

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.manager.DatabaseManager
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class DatabaseManager extends Object implements AutoCloseable
The entry point that builds named connections from a DatabaseConfig the first time each is used and hands out their Connection, QueryFactory, Schema and Migrator.Builder.

Each name is built once, even when several threads ask at the same moment, and building one name never blocks another. The manager keeps what the Connector built until purge(String), disconnect(String) or close().

Instances are safe to share between threads. Closing the manager, or purging a name, while another thread still runs a statement on that connection closes the connection under it; that statement may fail with the driver's own error, as it does in Laravel.

API Note:
The manager does not pool: without a registered data source a connector builds a plain one from the config, and every session opens its own physical connection. A server that needs a pool registers one with DatabaseManager.Builder.dataSource(String, Supplier).

    • migrator

      public Migrator.Builder migrator(String name)
      Starts a migrator on a named connection, with that connector's lock when it has one.

      The connection is also added under its own name, so a migration that names it through Migration.connection() runs there.

      Parameters:
      name - the connection name, never null
      Returns:
      a migrator builder to add migrations to, already carrying the manager's migration listeners, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if name is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if no connection or no connector matches
      IllegalStateException - if the manager is closed

    • usingConnection

      public <R> R usingConnection(String name, Supplier<R> work)
      Runs work with another connection as this thread's default, then restores it.

      Only the calling thread is affected; other threads keep their default. The previous default returns when the work ends, normally or by an exception.

      Type Parameters:
      R - the type of the result
      Parameters:
      name - the name of a configured connection, never null
      work - the work, never null
      Returns:
      the result of work, may be null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if no connection has that name
      IllegalStateException - if the manager is closed

    • purge

      public void purge(String name)
      Closes a connection and forgets it; the next use builds a new one from the same config.

      Does nothing when the name was never built.

      Parameters:
      name - the connection name, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if name is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if no connection has that name
      IllegalStateException - if the manager is closed, or the connector or a registered data source failed to close

    • disconnect

      public void disconnect(String name)
      Closes a connection like purge(String).

      Laravel keeps the connection object and drops only its PDO; here the config is what persists, so both calls end in the same state.

      Parameters:
      name - the connection name, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if name is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if no connection has that name
      IllegalStateException - if the manager is closed, or closing failed

    • close

      public void close()
      Closes every built connection. Calling it again does nothing.

      Every holder is closed even when one fails; the first failure is thrown after the rest, with later ones attached as suppressed. Afterwards every other method throws IllegalStateException.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if a connector or a registered data source failed to close
